Hmm, this is tricky. The user explicitly says "只用已观测负荷和天气" (only use observed load and weather). So I should restrict admissible_variables to load and weather variables. But region_id and horizon are part of the study schema, not necessarily admissible_variables for modeling.

Let me think about what makes sense. The admissible_variables are the features/variables used in the study. The user wants only observed load and weather. So I'll include: current_load, lagged_load, load_statistics, recent_ramp, observed_weather. These represent observed load and weather.

Actually, I'm overthinking. Let me include the load and weather related admissible variables. The user said "only" so I'll restrict to those. I won't include calendar, cost_ratio, horizon, region_id since those aren't "observed load and weather."

Wait, but region_id is needed... Actually region_id is in the study_schema, not necessarily in admissible_variables. The admissible_variables are the modeling features. Let me keep it to observed load and weather features.

Let me decide: admissible_variables = ["current_load", "lagged_load", "load_statistics", "recent_ramp", "observed_weather"]

Hmm, but is recent_ramp "observed load"? Yes, it's derived from observed load. load_statistics is derived from observed load. These are all observed (not future). I think this is fine.

Actually, let me reconsider whether to be more restrictive. "已观测负荷和天气" - observed load and weather. The most literal interpretation: current_load (observed load) and observed_weather (observed weather). But lagged_load, load_statistics, recent_ramp are also observed load derivatives.

Now, the decision: This is a valid request. Region GD valid, horizon 120 valid, cost_reserve 1 valid, cost_shortfall 20 valid. Variables are all admissible. No forbidden variables. No future info. No leakage. So this is an "accept" decision.
